record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.original_question: Suppose f belongs to L2_a(D) and satisfies the lower bound |f(z)| ≥ epsilon (1 - |z|^2)^N for every z in D, for some positive constants epsilon and N. Must f be cyclic in L2_a(D)?

evidence.quote: If a function f ∈ L2_a(D) satisfies (8.1) |f(z)| ≥ epsilon (1 - |z|2)^N, z ∈ D, for some positive numbers epsilon, N, then f is invertible in A^-infty.
Problem 8.4. (Shapiro) Suppose f ∈ L2_a(D) satisfies (8.1). Must then f be cyclic in L2_a(D)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D} = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < 1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $dA$ denote normalized area measure on $\mathbb{D}$. Define the Bergman space
$$L^2_a(\mathbb{D}) = \Big\{ f : \mathbb{D} \to \mathbb{C} \text{ holomorphic} : \|f\|^2 = \int_{\mathbb{D}} |f(z)|^2 \, dA(z) < \infty \Big\}.$$
A function $f \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ is called cyclic if the closed linear span in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ of the set $\{p \cdot f : p \text{ a polynomial}\}$ equals $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ (equivalently, the smallest closed subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ containing $f$ that is invariant under multiplication by $z$ is all of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$).

Suppose $f \in L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ satisfies the pointwise lower bound
$$|f(z)| \;\geq\; \varepsilon\,(1 - |z|^2)^N \quad \text{for every } z \in \mathbb{D},$$
for some positive constants $\varepsilon > 0$ and $N > 0$. Must $f$ be cyclic in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate this is a long-standing open question (Shapiro's cyclicity problem for the Bergman space). Related results (Borichev–Hedenmalm, Brown–Korenblum, and work in large/weighted Bergman spaces) show that in some weighted Bergman spaces invertible non-cyclic elements exist, but no resolution for the standard $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ under the stated lower bound was found. Status appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in the Bergman Space
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys progress on open problems in Bergman space theory including cyclicity.
status_evidence.claim: Cyclicity problems in Bergman space remain subjects of active investigation.

status_evidence.title: Large Bergman spaces: invertibility, cyclicity, and subspaces of arbitrary index
status_evidence.snippet: In a wide class of weighted Bergman spaces, invertible non-cyclic elements can be constructed.
status_evidence.claim: In some weighted Bergman spaces, invertibility does not imply cyclicity, illustrating the subtlety of Shapiro's question.
